name: WarehouseFlow New
description: Synthetic warehouse receiving, dispatch, stock-audit and handling records.

tables.definition: Warehouse identity, capacity and database maintenance times. These maintenance times do not document warehouse work.

columns.name: warehouse_id
columns.definition: Unique warehouse identity; foreign references identify the warehouse concerned.

columns.name: warehouse_name
columns.definition: English warehouse name.

columns.name: capacity
columns.definition: Maximum stored stock units for the simulated warehouse.

columns.name: created_at
columns.definition: UTC database record-creation time, not a warehouse business action.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.definition: UTC database maintenance time, not a warehouse business action.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE warehouse(warehouse_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, warehouse_name TEXT NOT NULL, capacity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(capacity>0), created_at TEXT NOT NULL, updated_at TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.definition: Goods identity and product category; NORMAL/FRAGILE describe the goods.

columns.name: goods_id
columns.definition: Unique goods identity; foreign references identify the goods concerned.

columns.name: goods_name
columns.definition: English goods name.

columns.name: category_code
columns.definition: NORMAL or FRAGILE product category, not an action.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE goods(goods_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, goods_name TEXT NOT NULL, category_code TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(category_code IN ('NORMAL','FRAGILE')))

tables.definition: Worker identity and job role. role_code identifies a role, not an action performed.

columns.name: worker_id
columns.definition: Unique worker identity; on a work or audit record, identifies the worker performing it.

columns.name: worker_name
columns.definition: English worker name.

columns.name: role_code
columns.definition: HANDLER or SUPERVISOR worker role, not the action performed.

columns.name: updated_at
columns.definition: UTC database maintenance time, not a warehouse business action.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE worker(worker_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, worker_name TEXT NOT NULL, role_code TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(role_code IN ('HANDLER','SUPERVISOR')), updated_at TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.definition: Business meanings of codes within the specified code family.

columns.name: code_family
columns.definition: Business context for the code. Each work table has one fixed family enforced by CHECK.

columns.name: code
columns.definition: Business code within the stated family.

columns.name: meaning
columns.definition: English business meaning of the code in its family.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE work_code(code_family TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(code_family IN ('MOVEMENT','REQUEST','TASK','HANDLING')), code TEXT NOT NULL, meaning TEXT NOT NULL, PRIMARY KEY(code_family,code))

tables.definition: One submitted request for receipt of one goods type into a warehouse.

columns.name: request_id
columns.definition: Unique receiving-request identity; foreign references identify the same request.

columns.name: warehouse_id
columns.definition: Unique warehouse identity; foreign references identify the warehouse concerned.

columns.name: goods_id
columns.definition: Unique goods identity; foreign references identify the goods concerned.

columns.name: quantity
columns.definition: Positive number of goods units requested or moved.

columns.name: submitted_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC receiving-request submission time.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE receiving_request(request_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, warehouse_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES warehouse(warehouse_id), goods_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES goods(goods_id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(quantity>0), submitted_at TEXT NOT NULL)

tables.definition: One actual receipt registration for a receiving request. condition_code describes goods condition, not the receipt action kind.

columns.name: receipt_id
columns.definition: Unique receipt-registration identity; on a stock movement, references its receipt registration.

columns.name: request_id
columns.definition: Unique receiving-request identity; foreign references identify the same request.

columns.name: receiver_id
columns.definition: Worker who registered the actual receipt.

columns.name: received_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC receipt-registration time.

columns.name: condition_code
columns.definition: GOOD or DAMAGED condition observed when goods were received. Either value denotes the same kind of receipt registration.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE goods_receipt(receipt_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, request_id TEXT NOT NULL UNIQUE REFERENCES receiving_request(request_id), receiver_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES worker(worker_id), received_at TEXT NOT NULL, condition_code TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(condition_code IN ('GOOD','DAMAGED')))

tables.definition: One request to dispatch one goods type, with separate actual request and approval times. Priority describes urgency.

columns.name: dispatch_id
columns.definition: Unique dispatch-order identity; foreign references identify the same dispatch request.

columns.name: warehouse_id
columns.definition: Unique warehouse identity; foreign references identify the warehouse concerned.

columns.name: goods_id
columns.definition: Unique goods identity; foreign references identify the goods concerned.

columns.name: quantity
columns.definition: Positive number of goods units requested or moved.

columns.name: priority_code
columns.definition: NORMAL or URGENT dispatch urgency; does not identify the action performed.

columns.name: requested_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC dispatch-request submission time.

columns.name: approved_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC dispatch-approval time; NULL if not yet approved.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE dispatch_order(dispatch_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, warehouse_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES warehouse(warehouse_id), goods_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES goods(goods_id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(quantity>0), priority_code TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(priority_code IN ('NORMAL','URGENT')), requested_at TEXT NOT NULL, approved_at TEXT, CHECK(approved_at IS NULL OR requested_at<approved_at))

tables.definition: One stock-audit occurrence, its actual start and completion, and its outcome. PASS/RECOUNT describes the result of the same audit kind.

columns.name: audit_id
columns.definition: Unique stock-audit occurrence identifier.

columns.name: warehouse_id
columns.definition: Unique warehouse identity; foreign references identify the warehouse concerned.

columns.name: worker_id
columns.definition: Unique worker identity; on a work or audit record, identifies the worker performing it.

columns.name: started_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC start time of this audit or work occurrence.

columns.name: completed_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC completion time of this audit or work occurrence; NULL if unfinished.

columns.name: result_code
columns.definition: PASS or RECOUNT outcome of a completed stock audit, or PENDING for an unfinished audit.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE warehouse_audit(audit_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, warehouse_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES warehouse(warehouse_id), worker_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES worker(worker_id), started_at TEXT NOT NULL, completed_at TEXT, result_code TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(result_code IN ('PASS','RECOUNT','PENDING')), CHECK((completed_at IS NULL AND result_code='PENDING') OR (completed_at IS NOT NULL AND started_at<completed_at AND result_code IN ('PASS','RECOUNT'))))

tables.definition: One completed inbound or outbound stock movement; each row records when the movement actually occurred.

columns.name: movement_id
columns.definition: Unique stock-movement occurrence identifier.

columns.name: warehouse_id
columns.definition: Unique warehouse identity; foreign references identify the warehouse concerned.

columns.name: goods_id
columns.definition: Unique goods identity; foreign references identify the goods concerned.

columns.name: quantity
columns.definition: Positive number of goods units requested or moved.

columns.name: receipt_id
columns.definition: Unique receipt-registration identity; on a stock movement, references its receipt registration.

columns.name: dispatch_id
columns.definition: Unique dispatch-order identity; foreign references identify the same dispatch request.

columns.name: code_family
columns.definition: Business context for the code. Each work table has one fixed family enforced by CHECK.

columns.name: movement_code
columns.definition: Physical business-action code in MOVEMENT context; I = Receipt into warehouse stock; O = Dispatch from warehouse stock. Recorded occurrence time is given by the corresponding event timestamp; the code alone is not proof of occurrence.

columns.name: occurred_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC time of this completed stock movement or request action.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE goods_movement(movement_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, warehouse_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES warehouse(warehouse_id), goods_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES goods(goods_id), quantity INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK(quantity>0), receipt_id TEXT UNIQUE REFERENCES goods_receipt(receipt_id), dispatch_id TEXT UNIQUE REFERENCES dispatch_order(dispatch_id), code_family TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'MOVEMENT' CHECK(code_family='MOVEMENT'), movement_code TEXT NOT NULL, occurred_at TEXT NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY(code_family,movement_code) REFERENCES work_code(code_family,code), CHECK((movement_code='IN' AND receipt_id IS NOT NULL AND dispatch_id IS NULL) OR (movement_code='OUT' AND receipt_id IS NULL AND dispatch_id IS NOT NULL)))

tables.definition: One checking, holding or releasing action performed on a receiving request; repeated checking actions retain separate records.

columns.name: action_id
columns.definition: Unique receiving-request action occurrence identifier.

columns.name: request_id
columns.definition: Unique receiving-request identity; foreign references identify the same request.

columns.name: worker_id
columns.definition: Unique worker identity; on a work or audit record, identifies the worker performing it.

columns.name: code_family
columns.definition: Business context for the code. Each work table has one fixed family enforced by CHECK.

columns.name: action_code
columns.definition: Physical business-action code in REQUEST context; A = Check receiving request; H = Hold receiving request; R = Release receiving request. Recorded occurrence time is given by the corresponding event timestamp; the code alone is not proof of occurrence.

columns.name: occurred_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC time of this completed stock movement or request action.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE request_action(action_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, request_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES receiving_request(request_id), worker_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES worker(worker_id), code_family TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'REQUEST' CHECK(code_family='REQUEST'), action_code TEXT NOT NULL, occurred_at TEXT NOT NULL, FOREIGN KEY(code_family,action_code) REFERENCES work_code(code_family,code))

tables.definition: One putaway, picking or packing work occurrence, with actual start and optional completion. A repeated attempt has a new task_id.

columns.name: task_id
columns.definition: Unique task-attempt identifier; repeat work has a new identifier.

columns.name: request_id
columns.definition: Unique receiving-request identity; foreign references identify the same request.

columns.name: dispatch_id
columns.definition: Unique dispatch-order identity; foreign references identify the same dispatch request.

columns.name: worker_id
columns.definition: Unique worker identity; on a work or audit record, identifies the worker performing it.

columns.name: code_family
columns.definition: Business context for the code. Each work table has one fixed family enforced by CHECK.

columns.name: task_code
columns.definition: Physical business-action code in TASK context; A = Putaway work; K = Picking work; B = Packing work. Recorded occurrence time is given by the corresponding event timestamp; the code alone is not proof of occurrence.

columns.name: started_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC start time of this audit or work occurrence.

columns.name: completed_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC completion time of this audit or work occurrence; NULL if unfinished.

columns.name: outcome_code
columns.definition: OK or RETRY result of a completed task attempt, or PENDING while unfinished; the outcome does not change the kind of work.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE warehouse_task_history(task_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, request_id TEXT REFERENCES receiving_request(request_id), dispatch_id TEXT REFERENCES dispatch_order(dispatch_id), worker_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES worker(worker_id), code_family TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'TASK' CHECK(code_family='TASK'), task_code TEXT NOT NULL, started_at TEXT NOT NULL, completed_at TEXT, outcome_code TEXT NOT NULL CHECK(outcome_code IN ('OK','RETRY','PENDING')), FOREIGN KEY(code_family,task_code) REFERENCES work_code(code_family,code), CHECK((task_code='PUTAWAY' AND request_id IS NOT NULL AND dispatch_id IS NULL) OR (task_code IN ('PICK','PACK') AND dispatch_id IS NOT NULL AND request_id IS NULL)), CHECK((completed_at IS NULL AND outcome_code='PENDING') OR (completed_at IS NOT NULL AND started_at<completed_at AND outcome_code IN ('OK','RETRY'))))

tables.definition: One unloading or loading occurrence, with actual start and optional completion. A repeated attempt has a new handling_id.

columns.name: handling_id
columns.definition: Unique handling-attempt identifier.

columns.name: request_id
columns.definition: Unique receiving-request identity; foreign references identify the same request.

columns.name: dispatch_id
columns.definition: Unique dispatch-order identity; foreign references identify the same dispatch request.

columns.name: worker_id
columns.definition: Unique worker identity; on a work or audit record, identifies the worker performing it.

columns.name: code_family
columns.definition: Business context for the code. Each work table has one fixed family enforced by CHECK.

columns.name: handling_code
columns.definition: Physical business-action code in HANDLING context; U = Unloading work; L = Loading work. Recorded occurrence time is given by the corresponding event timestamp; the code alone is not proof of occurrence.

columns.name: started_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC start time of this audit or work occurrence.

columns.name: completed_at
columns.definition: Actual UTC completion time of this audit or work occurrence; NULL if unfinished.

tables.sql_definition: CREATE TABLE handling_history(handling_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY NOT NULL, request_id TEXT REFERENCES receiving_request(request_id), dispatch_id TEXT REFERENCES dispatch_order(dispatch_id), worker_id TEXT NOT NULL REFERENCES worker(worker_id), code_family TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'HANDLING' CHECK(code_family='HANDLING'), handling_code TEXT NOT NULL, started_at TEXT NOT NULL, completed_at TEXT, FOREIGN KEY(code_family,handling_code) REFERENCES work_code(code_family,code), CHECK((handling_code='UNLOAD' AND request_id IS NOT NULL AND dispatch_id IS NULL) OR (handling_code='LOAD' AND dispatch_id IS NOT NULL AND request_id IS NULL)), CHECK(completed_at IS NULL OR started_at<completed_at))

business_rules: Each receiving request and dispatch order concerns one goods type in one warehouse; quantities are positive. This sample does not model multi-line orders.
One actual receipt registration can exist for each receiving request. Actual stock posting is recorded separately.
Each movement refers either to an inbound receipt or an outbound dispatch, with the same warehouse and goods context.
Every work attempt and audit retains its own start and optional completion times. Unfinished work has no completion time.
Repeated task attempts and request checks retain separate occurrence identifiers.
Goods category, dispatch urgency, goods condition, worker role, audit result and task outcome describe their respective business contexts rather than different kinds of action.
A handling/task occurrence refers either to a receiving request or to a dispatch order as constrained by its work kind.
All rows, code conventions, times and quantities are synthetic.

Business-action codes are namespace-specific. Identical physical codes in different business contexts can mean different actions. Use the code's business definition or referenced code table; do not infer meaning from the raw code alone.
